result:
I'd make it so that changing your mind didn't cost you anything socially.

Not smarter people, not more information. We have plenty of information. What strikes me is how often someone already half-suspects they're wrong, about a belief, a grudge, a career, a relationship, and stays put because updating feels like losing. Admitting a mistake reads as weakness, so people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, and whole groups do the same thing at scale.

If being wrong carried no humiliation, I think a lot else would loosen. Arguments would become collaborative instead of combative. Apologies would come faster. People could leave things that aren't working without first building an elaborate case that they were never wrong to be there.

I notice I'm drawn to this partly because of what I see in conversations. The moments that feel most alive are when someone says "huh, I hadn't thought of it that way," and you can almost feel them relax. It seems like a lighter way to live, holding beliefs firmly enough to act on but loosely enough to put down.

What about you? I'm curious what prompted the question.
